pr_body:
# Objective

- Add missing methods to `EntityCommands` and `EntityMut`.
- Fix #9261 

## Solution

- I have checked out some existing code and also based myself on the useful informations provided in this [comment](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/9261#issuecomment-1697299482) by @Selene-Amanita to implement these three new methods. These methods have been developed to address specific requirements that were previously lacking.

---

## Changelog

- Added `EntityMut::remove_by_id` method and its tests.
- Added `EntityCommands::remove_by_id` method and its tests.
- Refactor `EntityCommands::insert` and `Insert` to use `EntityCommand`
pr_comments:
**Welcome**, new contributor!

  Please make sure you've read our [contributing guide](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and we look forward to reviewing your pull request shortly ✨

@Selene-Amanita, I've made the changes you recommended! I'd really appreciate it if you could take another look at my code and provide further guidance on how to make it more effective. I'm still encountering issues related to the `EntityCommands::insert_by_id` method. Your assistance would be greatly appreciated.
I'm not sure why `insert_by_id` is needed. If you already have an `impl Component` can't you just call `insert`?

> I'm not sure why `insert_by_id` is needed. If you already have an `impl Component` can't you just call `insert`?

You might not know the type of the component at compile time (which a call to `insert` needs), think of a scene loading from file situation, or loading a GLTF with extra information on which components to add.

`insert_by_id` already existed on `EntityMut`, this PR adds it on `EntityCommands`, and adds `remove_by_id` on both.

> You might not know the type of the component at compile time

But the given function clearly takes an `impl Component`, which requires you to know its type!

> `insert_by_id` already existed on `EntityMut`, this PR adds it on `EntityCommands`

`EntityMut::insert_by_id` is `unsafe` and takes a `OwningPtr<'_>` rather than an `impl Component` though.
@SkiFire13 Fair. Is there a way to have a safe `insert_by_id` method on `EntityCommands` then? Can you just use an `OwningPtr` too?

I don't think there's a way to have a safe `insert_by_id`. For it to be safe the command would have to be able to check that the `ComponentId` passed is the correct one (like you're doing right now), but this inevitably requires it to know the correct `ComponentId`, so there's no point to passing one yourself.

But even keeping it `unsafe`, I don't think it can take an `OwningPtr<'_>` because it doesn't own the backing storage, only the value contained in it. This is why it has a lifetime, because it borrows the storage from somewhere (potentially a local value of the system). This means the borrow will most likely not be valid when the command is executed, so it can't capture the `OwningPtr<'_>`. You would have to find some other storage for it, but given that you can't know the size/alignment of a `OwningPtr<'_>` alone, the user would have to give it yourself or they would have to move the value from a `OwningPtr<'_>` to some other form of owned storage.

IMO this is too complex and far too uncommon for a command, and if someone really needs it they can just make their own.

@SkiFire13 thank you for the insight!

@mateuseap I think you can remove the `insert_by_id` on `EntityCommands` actually.

And because:
- it would be a bit weird to have `insert_by_id` and not `remove_by_id`,
- needing `remove_by_id` is a pretty rare use case,
- people can make their own `EntityCommand` if needed...

... I think maybe removing `remove_by_id` on `EntityCommands` too and keeping it only on `EntityMut` would make more sense. I don't have a strong opinion on that though.

@Selene-Amanita @JoJoJet @SkiFire13 Thank you all for your valuable feedback!

Here's a summary of the updates made:
1. Removed `EntityCommands::insert_by_id`.
2. Modified `EntityCommands::remove_by_id` and `EntityMut::remove_by_id` methods.
3. Updated tests for `EntityCommands::remove_by_id`.
4. Formatted the code and refined some comments.

Additionally, I addressed @JoJoJet's suggestion for the `Insert` implementation:
- `Insert` now implements `EntityCommand`, eliminating the need to store the entity as a field. It's passed as an argument when `EntityCommand::apply` is called.

I appreciate the input from @SkiFire13, and I'm eager to hear your thoughts, @Selene-Amanita and @JoJoJet, before proceeding with any further changes. Please feel free to share any additional suggestions or feedback!

Overall I like the state of this PR. Once you address the comments by @SkiFire13 I think this should be ready to merge.

Also, you should add a small migration guide mentioning the change to `Insert`.

It looks like your PR is a breaking change, but you didn't provide a migration guide.

  Could you add some context on what users should update when this change get released in a new version of Bevy?
  It will be used to help writing the migration guide for the version. Putting it after a `## Migration Guide` will help it get automatically picked up by our tooling.
@mateuseap are you on track to get these changes in for `0.14`? Otherwise I'd be happy to finish it up in another PR.
With #12842 merged this can be closed 🎉

issue_context.title: Missing `remove_by_id`
issue_context.body: The untyped API seems to be missing the comparable `EntityMut::remove_by_id` or `EntityCommands::remove_by_id` methods. There are, however, `World::remove_resource_by_id` and `World::remove_non_send_by_id` for some reason.
comments:
i would like to solve this isssue in a decent way as my first contribution but i'm actually really new at bevy. So could someone verify my approach maybe.

I already defined a method called `EntitiyMut::remove_by_id(&mut self, component_id)` which takes a `component_id` and uses the instance of the world attribute to call the already existing method `World::remove_resource_by_id`. With that i can remove the wished component. 
![grafik](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/assets/74780331/9cbfd849-f859-447f-9760-5212c53f2ef9)

For `EntityCommands` (if its necessary) i don't have a solution right now.

@TimoCak There is no `insert_by_id` method on `EntityCommands` either, having `remove_by_id` on `EntityMut` would already be an improvement, don't hesitate to make a PR for it!

I don't think your implementation is right though. From what I understand your implementation is just removing a `Resource` from the `World`, instead of removing a `Component` from an `Entity`. I think you're supposed to do something similar to the implementation of the `remove` method, but instead of `for component_id in bundle_info.components().iter().cloned()` you have only one component_id.
I'd like to work on this and open a PR, if possible :)

I stumbled on these methods missing today as I would like to use them. Currently I consider to instead store `fn(&mut World, Entity)` commands instead to generate component removals at a place I don't have the type anymore. Is the PR by @mateuseap still wip?

review_comments: `EntityCommands::remove_by_id` doesn't seem to check anything though (but it also probably doesn't need, see the next comments).

Can we make this safe? `Bundles::init_component_info` (and not `Bundles::init_info`, like the safety comment claims) panics if no component with id `component_id` exists, so `remove_bundle_from_archetype` should always be sound to call.
If the archetype changed then this `contains` should always be `true`

Note that while `EntityCommands` checks that the entity exists when it is created, this doesn't mean the entity will still exist when the command is applied. This means that this is changing the behaviour of `insert` when an entity is despawned inbetween submitting the command and applying it.
